analysis:
Examined the head text of EngineV2Bridge+Submission.swift and the Translation patch and base. The PR adds a fail-fast refusal in submitTokenized (lines 154-158). Native-tracked engines now reject logprobs and token constraints with a typed unsupportedOutputControl error instead of an SDK-internal failure. The non-throwing wrapper (lines 96-101) maps it back to an in-band error stream. Translation adds the constant unsupportedOutputControlPrefix.

Security-relevant observations:
- The refusal runs after canSubmitWithNativeOwner and before any resource acquisition, so no service allowance, KV reservation, prefix receipt, SSD staging, pendingSubmissionIDs entry or idMap entry exists yet. Nothing leaks. The only cleanup needed is usageSignal.finalizeLookup(.policy), which is called.
- A refusal before cache staging means the request does no cache lookup, donation or ready-receipt registration. T-041 cache scoping and the TTFT oracle are unchanged. The check is purely request-shape based and does not touch cacheScope.
- The error text is a fixed content-free string with no prompt material, which is consistent with the T-008 and T-050 posture. A client-induced refusal is now a typed 400 and no longer an untyped 500 that trips the coordinator's inference-error breaker. This is a small availability improvement for T-010 style DoS against provider reputation.
- The continuation is finished before the throw, so the stream is not left dangling.
- When the throw is caught in the non-throwing wrapper, finalizeLookup runs only once, because the thrower already called it. A double call is idempotent in this design as far as the supplied code shows.

Unverified contracts outside the supplied evidence: the definition of MultiModelBatchSchedulerEngineError.unsupportedOutputControl and its fromSchedulerMessage mapping to 400 (the Translation comment claims it). Also the callers of the throwing overload, which must handle the new case without leaking a stream. I found no concrete regression.
